tagline: A control tower for your Claude agents.

colors.note: Every value below is read from source. Brand amber/red are hard-coded in src/Glyph.swift and Tower Identity Study.html. Neutrals (ink/paper/surface/muted) are from the identity study CSS :root. macOS system colors are the literal sRGB values NSColor resolves to (app uses Color(nsColor:...)), captured for Dark and Light appearance.

amber_hold.role: warn / held-pending (holdNet, holdGeo); TUI C_WARN semantic

red_danger.role: danger / unguarded (radar off state), destructive confirm

text_primary.role: primary text / paper; also the default glyph currentColor

model_tier_accents.note: Text-label only. DESIGN.md: 'appears only in the row's small text label — never on the mark itself.' Marks are monochrome.

status_semantics.note: src/DesignSystem.swift AgentStatus.color uses NSColor system colors; hexes are the resolved sRGB values on this machine (macOS 26 / Darwin 25.5).

tui_palette.note: src/tower-tui.py init_colors() — 8-color curses pairs on the terminal's own default background (use_default_colors, bg = -1). These are role names, not hexes; render with the terminal-ANSI equivalents below if the video shows the TUI.

video_palette_recommendation.rule: amber and red are load-bearing (hold vs unguarded) — never use them decoratively

radar_glyph.summary: Tower's mark: a radar on a control tower. One geometry, five states = the guard. Drawn in a 0..100 box; identical in src/Glyph.swift drawRadar() and the SVG in Tower Identity Study.html.

coordinate_system.angles: degrees, 0 deg = +x axis, increasing clockwise on screen (because y is down). Pillow arc() uses the same convention.

states.name: clear
states.means: guarding · in-country + path to Anthropic open

motion.name: rotating sweep with a soft trail

trail.shape: wedge: hub -> arc of r=33 sampled at 13 points from 270deg to 208.5deg -> close

motion.reduce_motion_still: sweep frozen at rotation 0 (needle straight up)

states.name: holdNet
states.means: no usable path (offline / captive / edge unreachable) — held pending, self-clears

states.name: holdGeo
states.means: wrong country / VPN — held, not failed

states.name: off
states.means: routing off — Claude connects directly, UNGUARDED. Danger.
states.core: HOLLOW red: stroke circle r=5.5, width 4, #E5484D (no fill)

motion.name: none — the off state is still

awake_vigil_overlay.note: Keep-awake rides ANY radar state; deliberately NEUTRAL (never amber/red) so a hold always outranks it. Drawn under the core.

beacon_standalone.note: src/Glyph.swift drawBeacon — the same lamp without the radar ring, 0..100 box.

radar_glyph.phase_variable: P = seconds (timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate). For a rendered video, P = frame_index / fps; all formulas are pure functions of (state, P).
pillow_notes: Draw at 4-8x supersample then LANCZOS-downsample: Pillow has no native antialiasing for ellipse/arc.
Dashes: Pillow has no dash support — synthesize by drawing arc() segments; e.g. dash [5,7] on r=33 means arc-length 5 on, 7 off, converted to degrees via deg = 360*len/(2*pi*r).
Strokes: ImageDraw.ellipse(..., width=w) strokes inward-centered; for exactness draw arcs with width=w on the r circle.
Alpha: composite each element as its own RGBA layer so overlapping opacities match the SwiftUI/SVG result.

model_marks.rule: Monochrome, drawn in the same 0..100 box (drawModelMark). Still at rest; alive only while that agent is working. The tier accent lives in the text label only.

haiku.form: three ticks at -90/30/150 deg from (16) to (34) radius, stroke 8 round + core circle r=7
haiku.motion: ticks breathe outward (osc = 0.5+0.5*sin(P*2.3 + k*2.094), offset E*3.4*osc); whole mark sways E*6*sin(P*0.7); core scales 1 + E*0.22*sin(P*3.0)

sonnet.form: one S stroke: upper arc center (50,37.5) r=12.5 bulging right, lower arc center (50,62.5) r=12.5 bulging left; stroke 8 round
sonnet.motion: slow continuous turn rot = E*(P*16) + E*4*sin(P*1.3); scale 1 + E*0.05*sin(P*1.3)

opus.form: three 300-deg open arcs at radii [16,27,38], gap starts [90,210,330] deg, stroke 6.5 + core r=5
opus.motion: each ring rotates at its own rate [14,-10,8] deg-units*P*E; core pulses 1 + E*0.18*sin(P*2.1)

fable.form: Archimedean-ish spiral, 120 steps, f in 0..1: angle = f*2.35*2pi - pi/2, r = 2.5 + 32.5*f; stroke 8 round + core r=4
fable.motion: a highlight segment winds up it: head = (P*0.22) mod 1, tail = head-0.16, stroke 8.6 at alpha 0.95, plus a dot r=5 at the head

three_rules: The mark is the state — the radar IS the guard, a model mark IS the model. Nothing decorative signals status.
Motion = state change — celebration is earned (done), never granted (failure is sober). Nothing loops at full attention when all is well.
One loudest thing — a strict attention hierarchy; at most one element pulses at a time.

tokens.radar_fps: ~30fps only while the state warrants it; live views are 60fps TimelineView, paused when idle

must_never: Failure must NEVER bounce — failed uses easeOut 0.25s, a sober fade. No spring, no overshoot, no shake.
Never more than one glowing/pulsing element at a time (newest wins).
The quiet state is completely still — nothing loops when all is well.
Never animate a state that has nothing to say (the radar freezes; the menu bar animates only for a hold, a verify sweep, or a calm scan while agents work).
Never reorder the popover sections — order encodes attention.
The menu bar never counts running agents (only the needs-you count, and optionally usage %).
motion_laws.reduce_motion: Always honored, no exceptions: loops stop, springs become 0.2s fades, counters set directly, and each radar state freezes at a legible STILL FRAME — never a blank. Every state above lists its reduce_motion_still values.
motion_laws.attention_hierarchy: menubar badge > Needs-You order > collision banner > the radar's own motion
motion_laws.dopamine_layer: Summary line ('3 at work · 41 jobs done today · 1 needs you') and per-row 'n ✓' counters tick up with numericText as agents complete tools; then quiet.

voice.register: Calm, factual, understated. Short declaratives. Says what is true, including when the news is bad. Never hypes.

lines.text: Tower — a control tower for your Claude agents.
Quiet tower, clear signal.
One daemon, four jobs: the agents, the weather, the fence, usage.
The fence — pin Claude Code to one country.
A tiny local proxy holds Claude's requests whenever you're not confirmed inside your target country.
Your country is confirmed every ~15 s against three independent geo providers.
A VPN drop is caught in about a quarter of a second, and a confirmation older than 60 s is never trusted.
The guard is fail-closed. There is no allow-through fallback.
An unconfirmed location never gets through.
A Claude request proceeds only when Tower can affirmatively confirm two things at once: you are inside the target country, and the network has a usable path to Anthropic.
A false hold is a pending retry that clears itself; a false allow is an off-country request you can't take back.
A held request is PENDING, not FAILED.
Tower holds it a few seconds, then answers 503 + Retry-After.
Claude Code turns a 503 into its own native "Retrying · attempt x/y" spinner.
The turn survives and resumes by itself the moment the guard clears.
Tower never returns 403 — Claude reads that as broken auth and kills the turn.
The weather — when Claude errors mid-session, Tower instantly answers: is it my internet, is it slow, or is it Anthropic?
Anthropic API unreachable — your internet is fine (23 ms).
A slow but reachable connection still gets through — degraded is not blocked.
Every running Claude Code agent, live: status, activity, model, momentum.
A ranked needs-you queue — failed > blocked > asking > done — with notifications, and click-to-focus that agent's terminal.
So none run off unwatched.
Statuses are derived read-only from Claude Code's own session transcripts — Tower never writes into ~/.claude and never injects input.
Your real plan usage, mirrored from claude -p /usage, plus a clearly-labeled local token/cost estimate.
The proxy tunnels HTTPS via CONNECT, so it sees each request's hostname — but never decrypts your traffic.
Turning the guard off is double-confirmed.
It always un-routes on shutdown, so Claude goes back to a direct connection.
One line. No password, no sudo, no Gatekeeper warning, nothing to drag or un-quarantine.
curl -fsSL https://ghhrmnzdh.github.io/tower/install.sh | sh

do_not_claim: Do NOT say Tower 'fails open', 'falls back to allowing', or 'lets traffic through when unsure'. It is fail-closed: uncertain = held. (CLAUDE.md, README.md)
Do NOT call Tower a VPN, proxy service, or IP changer. It does not change, hide, or relocate your IP — it only confirms where you already are and holds requests when you're not there.

Do NOT claim it guards anything other than Claude Code. It is Claude-Code-only; routing works because Claude Code obeys the proxy env in ~/.claude/settings.json. No browser Claude.ai, no other AI CLIs, no general apps.
Do NOT call it a firewall, kill switch, or OS-level protection. README: 'this is a proxy, not an OS-level kill switch… a program told to ignore the proxy could still reach the network.'
Do NOT say blocked requests 'fail', 'error out', or return 403. They are held, then answered 503 + Retry-After, and stay PENDING in Claude Code's own retry spinner. Tower never returns 403.
Do NOT say Tower inspects, decrypts, or reads your traffic or prompts. CONNECT tunneling means hostname only.
Do NOT say Tower reads your Claude token/credentials. Claude does the auth; network probes never touch credentials and never go through the proxy.
Do NOT say Tower controls, writes to, or injects into your Claude sessions. It is read-only toward ~/.claude session transcripts.
Do NOT say Tower edits your shell, adds aliases, or wraps the `claude` command. It only writes env keys into ~/.claude/settings.json.
Do NOT claim a slow connection is blocked. 'Degraded' (high-latency but reachable) still allows traffic; only offline / captive / edge-unreachable is a hold.
Do NOT claim the menu bar shows a running-agent count. It shows the needs-you count (switchable off) and optionally usage %.
Do NOT present 'waiting for approval' as certain — README calls it 'an honest heuristic (a pending tool call with a stalled transcript can also be a slow tool)'.
Do NOT claim it is notarized, App-Store-signed, or Apple-verified. It is ad-hoc signed and not notarized (that's why the install is a curl line).
Do NOT claim Windows support as shipped/stable. The daemon + TUI are experimental and have never been run on real Windows hardware; there is no native tray.
Do NOT claim Intel Mac, older macOS, or Linux support. Requirements: macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon, Python 3.8+, Claude Code installed.
Do NOT claim a cloud service, account, telemetry, or third-party dependencies. Stdlib + AppKit/SwiftUI only; nothing leaves the machine but the public-IP country lookup and network probes.
Do NOT claim it needs root or installs system-wide daemons (the only exception is the optional, opt-in keep-awake lid-closed mode, which asks for admin once and is fully removable).
Do NOT show plan-usage numbers while the guard is holding. When /usage is gated the front-ends show an honest message naming the cause (connection vs location) — never stale numbers.
Do NOT frame a hold, an amber radar, or a block as the app being broken. It is the app doing its job and reporting the truth; it clears itself when the condition recovers.
Do NOT show failure bouncing, springing, or celebrating. Failure is sober (easeOut 0.25s) — never a bounce.
Do NOT tint the model marks with their tier accent, and do NOT render the menu-bar radar as a flat monochrome template — the amber/red are the information.
Do NOT have two things pulsing at once, or any looping motion in the all-clear state.
